payload.scope:
TWO HALVES, and the second is the one that matters more.

HALF A - THE LANE WINS ON MERIT. ripgrep becomes a first-class dependency and the hand-rolled searcher is DELETED rather than kept beside it (owner ruling: no untested duplicate). Search gains context windows, globs, multiline, counts and caps through rg's --json event stream. se_file_read gains offset/limit. A record search spans refs - iter/* tags for shipped iterations, and main for v1, which is a branch of this repository rather than an external system. se_file_patch gains batch ops. Required args are enforced at dispatch instead of coerced. se_run stops being an invisible writer to the product. A machine-local config lane (se_config) serves the pairing, the brief store and root paths. Declared roots with @name addressing cover what is genuinely outside the repo.

HALF B - THE MACHINE JUDGES WHAT IT CAN JUDGE. Guidance stops being a hand-written paragraph per state: applicable rules are joined onto the packet by applies_to and their wikilinks resolved, so a law minted today binds a session tomorrow. Every machine-state check is sorted into MECHANICAL or JUDGEMENT, lint infrastructure is built where it does not exist, and everything mechanical is linted - starting with models-adhered, red-observed, designs-realized, adrs-traced, verify-method presence and breaks-if-removed presence. The state-of-the-art scan becomes COLLECTED EVIDENCE rather than instructed prose, which is the specific gap this iteration's own retro found.

AND THE RECORD SURVIVES CARELESSNESS: annotated tags at close (lightweight tags are silently dropped by push.followTags), existing tags reworked, evidence_commit recorded beside evidence_tag, push.followTags set idempotently, iter/* branches deleted after close - which also resolves a ref-name ambiguity git already warns about, since a closed iteration currently has a branch AND a tag of the same name.
payload.non_goals:
- SEMANTIC OR VECTOR SEARCH over product files: rejected on freshness, not cost - an index tolerates staleness by design, and the agent reads back what it just wrote.
- ast-grep AND STRUCTURAL SEARCH: consciously deferred with a trigger, not overlooked - adopt when exact search stops answering, which for one TypeScript codebase it has not.
- A FALLBACK SEARCHER beside ripgrep: ruled out by the owner - duplicate code that is never tested and never run is worse than depending on rg outright.
- REPLACING se_get_search: BM25 over ledger nodes is a different job and is genuinely better than grep for guidance; it stays.
- LINTING JUDGEMENT: a lint judges facts, never intent - a check that needs more information stays prose rather than becoming a bad refusal.
- THE BOARD's remaining surface work: routed to i9, including the tab-per-start defect.
- THE PHONE LANE's cross-surface invalidation and the hosted page's false 'Blessed': routed to the next phone iteration.
- THE TOP-LEVEL MACHINE REWORK: reserved as i11 by the owner.
- CLOSING se.raid-an-iteration-cannot-run-its-own-build: it has now cost real time three times in one day and deserves scope, but not here - this iteration cannot fix the mechanism it is running inside without becoming two iterations.
- SEARCHING NON-TEXT CORPORA (PDFs, the college archive) via rg's -z and --pre: real capability, no current demand; recorded so a later iteration knows it comes free.
- MIGRATING THE REMOTE's existing lightweight tags: the local retag is in scope; the force-push that completes it is an owner act under se.rule-owner-pushes and ships as a handover step.
